title: Model companies mine the ore, product companies smelt it
dek: The best models capture the largest share of traffic and revenue, but the mining window is shrinking: from two years to nine months to three or four months. Foundation model companies are starting to build Agents end to end, and the cost disadvantage for application companies is structural.
why: Guangmi's seventh quarterly report, and this time it goes heavy on product. Divergence, the everything-bundle, vertical integration, L4 experience, the mining window — all five judgments are backed by specific numbers.
who: People watching AI investment and startups, especially founders and investors who want to know how application companies survive once foundation model companies start doing product.
skip: After 55:53, the section on US financial seigniorage and Chinese entrepreneurship is lower in information density.

points.h: Model companies are diverging, and only two are still doing general
points.body: Guangmi's most striking impression is that models are diverging: going forward, maybe only Google Gemini and OpenAI will truly do general models, wanting every capability — from multimodal to reasoning models to Coding to Agentic to 2C, and Google even wants to do world models. Other model companies have started to diverge into various domains — Anthropic into Coding and Agentic, and Mira's Thinking Machines Lab wants to do multimodal and next-generation interaction. This divergence isn't forced; it's a deliberate bet.

points.h: Anthropic was pushed all-in by positive feedback
points.body: Anthropic has almost given up multimodal, given up 2C, and hasn't pushed an independent reasoning model. Guangmi judges the turning point was the summer of 2024 when Claude 3.5 launched: feedback from outside developers gave the team a lot of positive reinforcement, and the whole team went more all-in on Coding and Agentic. He used the term ‘Reward Hacking’ — the management team may also have been Reward Hacked by Coding. The payoff on this bet: at the end of 2023 AR was probably under $100 million, in 2024 probably $950 million, and some speculate that annualized revenue in 2025 will exceed $12 billion, and maybe $30-40 billion in 2026.

points.h: Doing only Coding can't support a grand narrative, so there's strong non-consensus here
points.body: Guangmi believes Anthropic's core is betting on Coding and Agentic. If Anthropic weren't focused, and did both multimodal and 2C like Google and OpenAI, a strategy of spreading pepper everywhere would be very dangerous. But conversely, if OpenAI and Google threw the whole company into all-in Coding, Anthropic would also be in danger. The problem is that when Google's and OpenAI's CEOs or management are asked whether they should all-in on just Coding as a single capability direction, the answer is always No — everyone feels that doing only Coding isn't enough to support a grand narrative. So there's still very strong non-consensus around Coding.

points.h: Coding and world models are actually one thing
points.body: Google DeepMind CEO Dennis described Google's world model Genie 3 as an infinitely extensible virtual womb that gestates AGI. Guangmi says Coding is also a virtual womb, and world models and Coding are actually one thing, just different paths. His argument: what separates humans from animals is language and the ability to create or use tools; language plus Code plus Agentic tool capability lets an Agent, in the digital world, perform every action a human performs on a computer or phone — that's already AGI. Making a front-end website or a PPT used to take many rounds of back-and-forth with a studio; now it's hundreds to thousands of steps of Agentic reasoning, and finally Coding generates the HTML.

points.h: Thinking Machines is the most expensive angel round in global history
points.body: Mira was previously OpenAI's CTO, and her Thinking Machines Lab is the most expensive angel round in global history: $2 billion raised at a $10 billion valuation. Guangmi thinks three points matter most. First, this is the strongest exit team in Silicon Valley in recent years, possibly stronger than today's xAI, more like a spin-off of OpenAI ChatGPT or Post Train plus the core Infra team — Meta's Zuckerberg wanted to spend $1.5 billion to poach one of them, and that Infra lead turned it down outright; not a single person was poached. Second, Mira was OpenAI's most core management, and knows what was done well and what was done badly. Third, Mira may be, globally, suited to be Apple's CEO — a product-first philosophy matches Apple.

points.h: xAI's massive compute hasn't gotten payback
points.body: Musk's biggest bet before was a single massive cluster, that compute could bring fundamental model improvement. But Guangmi says there's no payback yet — massive compute can only be described as the baseline for not falling behind, but it doesn't necessarily let Grok overtake. Grok today is still groping for its own ecological niche: doing chat can't beat ChatGPT, doing search there's still Google and perplexity ahead, doing coding there's Anthropic, doing multimodal and world models — it feels like Grok today hasn't thought it through. Guangmi guesses xAI will very likely merge into Tesla as one integrated entity in the next half year to a year, because an independent AI Lab without a big leg to stand on is actually very hard.

points.h: Horizontal everything-bundles and vertical integration are happening at the same time
points.body: Guangmi says there are two most obvious trends today. One is the horizontal everything-bundle: with ChatGPT, you spend 20 bucks or 200 bucks for one account, and it already includes chat, search, coding, agent, workspace PPT — equal to buying a dozen suites, which is very bad for suites doing a single vertical capability. The other is vertical integration: Google Gemini goes from TPU chips to the Gemini model to the agent applications above it, plus Google Docs, Chrome browser, the Android operating system, YouTube video — it can do super-inheritance. So it's fine for Google Gemini to be a few months behind on model, especially since it isn't behind right now.

points.h: The mining window is shrinking: from two years to nine months to three months
points.body: Guangmi had a colleague specifically pull the window periods, and found the window is shrinking. Perplexity's window was two years — model companies themselves started adding web search on average two years late, but today ChatGPT has added web search and Perplexity is still maintaining high-speed growth, maybe still tens of millions of new users per month. Cursor got hot because of Claude's Sonnet, and from when Cursor started getting hot to the release of Claude Code was actually just nine months. Minus's window was launching this March or April, and ChatGPT following up with a similar product was about three to four months. From two years, one year, nine months, three months — the window is shrinking.

points.h: Cursor's long-term competition is very pessimistic
points.body: Guangmi says if he were the Cursor team, having to compete long-term with Claude Code today is actually very pessimistic. Suppose Cursor could immediately reproduce a product effect like Claude Code — it would still face such a high loss rate: product pricing is just 200 a month, but many users sometimes burn through thousands of yuan of tokens in a few days, even a token loss rate of 1 to 3 or even 1 to 10, and the cost is unbearable, easily dragged to death. And that's without even discussing how to optimize model capability later — if Cursor wants to change some capability or data distribution underneath, its model training capability can't keep up.

points.h: Bullish on Google again, because of scale effects
points.body: Guangmi's big change this time is being bullish on Google again. His observation is that ChatGPT and Google will ultimately converge on the same product form, like Xiaohongshu (小红书) fusing search, short video and a friends feed. Another guess is that ChatGPT will definitely do advertising later, because it just hired a new commercialization CEO, previously Instagram's CEO, and before that the lead of Meta's ad system. Maybe top users will be charged very expensively in the future, 200 a month, 2000 a month, but paying users may only be 3% to 5%, and over 95% of users are free, so it comes down to advertising. Google is still the world's best advertising platform.

terms.def: When a model or team is steered by short-term positive feedback into over-optimizing one direction.

quotes.text: Actually I think Coding is also a virtual womb — world models and Coding are really one thing.

Model companies — people spent tens of billions of dollars on model training, like mining, mining this intelligence ore. Then you find that after I mined the ore, the front-end application Cursor is raking in money hand over fist. Damn it, model companies aren't stupid either — I'm definitely going forward to harvest.
From two years, one year, nine months, three months — actually, the window is shrinking.
If Cursor or coding companies don't do models, they'll have no advantage in the future. In the future I think it's all about competing on cost advantage.
I think there's a very good summary: Jewish finance, Chinese AGI.
